idea-plugin.name: Sightline
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code inside Android Studio, with visible project activity and controlled tool execution.

Sightline provides a native Android Studio interface for a locally installed Claude Code CLI.

Use it to:

  • Chat with Claude without leaving Android Studio.
  • Attach files and IDE context, and remove any of it before you send.
  • Review tool requests and proposed changes as diffs before they apply.
  • Stop a turn without losing the conversation, and pick up where you left off.
  • Watch what a subagent is doing inside the task that started it.
  • Run your own Claude Code commands, skills and plugins from the panel.
  • See files, commands, tests and relationships in the Activity Map.
  • Inspect structured build, test and diagnostic results.

Android-aware. Sightline knows your build variant, connected device, module and running process, so you don't have to explain them. It reads Gradle failures into typed diagnoses, resolves crashes back to the line that threw, picks the tests worth running for what you changed, and audits your merged manifest. Logcat is redacted before it can reach a prompt.

Requires the Claude Code CLI (the claude command), installed and authenticated separately. Sightline does not provide Claude access, does not handle your credentials, and has no login screen or backend of its own.

No telemetry. No analytics, no usage statistics, nothing sent anywhere except to the local claude process you started. Sightline itself writes no transcript; note that the Claude Code CLI keeps its own session history under ~/.claude/projects/, under your account and its own retention rules, which is what lets a conversation resume.

Sightline is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, JetBrains or Google. "Claude" and "Claude Code" are trademarks of Anthropic; "Android Studio" is a trademark of Google. Both are used only to describe compatibility.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.8.1 — the first stable release since 0.7.0, after a pass in a live IDE.

Stop keeps your conversation. Stop now ends the turn instead of ending the CLI, so the session, its MCP servers and everything Claude knows survive — your next message just carries on. Press it again to end the process outright. A command Claude already started keeps running either way, and Sightline now says so rather than implying your build stopped.

The permission mode chip now works mid-conversation. Changing it used to save the setting and nothing else, leaving the chip showing a policy that was not actually in force.

You can see inside a Task. Subagents used to render as a wall of raw JSON. You now get what was delegated, the steps the subagent takes as it takes them, and what it concluded.

Your Claude Code commands are in the actions menu — built-ins, your project's own commands, and your plugins' skills, with their descriptions. Some, like /context, cost no tokens at all.

Claude can finally use the Android tools. They were registered on an MCP server the CLI filters down to a single tool, so none of them had ever been callable. They are served under their own name now.

Compaction and rate limits are reported. Both used to pass silently — which is why Claude could seem to forget something you told it earlier, with nothing on screen to explain it.

New, off by default: revert Claude's file changes. Right-click a message you sent to restore the files Claude edited since. It covers edits made with Edit, Write and NotebookEdit — not changes made by a command it ran, and not a subagent's edits inside a Task — and it repeats that every time it asks you to confirm.

The panel now opens on the conversation, not a split. At a typical docked width the old default left the chat column narrower than its own readable minimum. The Activity Map is one click away on the header switch, and whichever view you pick is remembered.

Corrected: this listing and the privacy notes said your conversation is never written to disk. Sightline writes no transcript, but the Claude Code CLI keeps its own session history under ~/.claude/projects/. Now stated plainly in both places.
